newsitem.title: UK: NWE fuel oil barges, low sulphur cargoes softer.
newsitem.headline: NWE fuel oil barges, low sulphur cargoes softer.

text.p: European high sulphur fuel oil barges closed steady on Tuesday with demand said to have improved from Monday, while low sulphur was said to have traded lower with weaker swaps.
High sulphur barges were unchanged from their earlier trading level of $85/$85.50 fob Rotterdam for RMG material and $86 for running refinery material -- all within Monday's trading range.
But demand was better than on Monday.
"Demand was reasonable, some 20,000 tonnes done today, which is a lot better than yesterday," one trader said.
Bunkers were traded at $87.50/$88 delivered for 380 cst material and 180 cst fetched some $5 higher.
No deals were heard in low sulphur barges, which continued last week's trend, offered at $97, with buyers $2 lower.
High sulphur cargoes continued to be offered steady at about $84/$85 cif with buyers at $81/$82, after swaps rose slightly over Monday's close.
But traders said one "problematic cargo" of high sulphur lower grade cracked material was on offer at $81 cif with bids no better than $79 cif.
